other.about: Cosmology and the cosmic web (G1; galaxy design sections 2 and 3): the universe's parameters, how the web's noise octaves are laid out, and what sets each epoch. A fictional universe pack may change any of them; everything downstream follows.

sources.haloes: Sheth and Tormen 1999 mass function and bias; growth M(z) = M0 (1+z)^alpha exp(beta z) (McBride et al. 2009) with alpha, beta from Correa et al. 2015 (paper I, MNRAS 450, 1514, doi:10.1093/mnras/stv689, eqs. 14, 15 and 20 to 23); spin Bullock et al. 2001 (the modified spin lambda prime, median 0.035; their classical lambda is 0.042); major mergers Fakhouri, Ma and Boylan-Kolchin 2010; formation scatter and environment shift are rough (sketch)
sources.params: The measured parameters (H0, Omega_b, Omega_c, Omega_m, sigma8, n_s, T_cmb, N_eff and the dark energy rows) moved to the master data sheet's Cosmos group in DM1 (packs/base-reference, Planck 2018 VI table 2); now_gyr is a model setting
sources.web: galaxy design section 3; T-web (Hahn et al. 2007) with its eigenvalue threshold set so 77% of space is void, the share measured by NEXUS+ in the Millennium simulation (Cautun et al. 2014, MNRAS 441, 2923, doi:10.1093/mnras/stu768); the threshold is found from Doroshkevich 1970's distribution of the tidal tensor for the smoothed Gaussian field, each draw weighted by the room the Zel'dovich step (Zel'dovich 1970) leaves it, so it is a share of space today, not of the matter, at every smoothing and epoch; voids then hold about 35 to 45% of the matter against the measured 15% (fudge register). Matter moved by the truncated Zel'dovich approximation (Coles, Melott and Shandarin 1993, MNRAS 260, 765), smoothed where the linear spread reaches 1 (Melott, Pellman and Shandarin 1994, MNRAS 269, 626)
sources.first_stars: 3-sigma peaks (our choice) of 1e6 solar-mass minihaloes (after Tegmark et al. 1997, whose 1e6 solar masses is baryonic, at z about 15; Barkana and Loeb 2001)
sources.cooling_mass_z9: virial temperature 1e4 K at z = 9 for mean molecular weight 0.6 (Barkana and Loeb 2001 eq. 26)
sources.reionisation_zeta: tuned so reionisation is half way at z = 7.7 (Planck 2018) and complete near z = 6 (Fan et al. 2006)
sources.far_future: Adams and Laughlin 1997, Rev. Mod. Phys. 69, 337; Hawking evaporation time from Page 1976. Speculative
sources.galaxy: Regulator model (Bouche et al. 2010; Lilly et al. 2013; Dave, Finlator and Oppenheimer 2012); depletion times Tacconi et al. 2018 and Leroy et al. 2008; winds Muratov et al. 2015; fallback Henriques et al. 2013; hot haloes and radio-mode feedback Croton et al. 2006; ex-situ growth Rodriguez-Gomez et al. 2016; ex-situ black holes at 1e-3 of the stars they arrive with, the bulge ratio of Kormendy and Ho 2013 (https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-astro-082708-101811; holes track bulges, and bulgeless galaxies hold 1e5 to 1e6 Msun holes); against total stellar mass Reines and Volonteri 2015 find 2.5e-4 for local hosts (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/813/2/82), so this runs high for disc-rich arrivals; discs Mo, Mao and White 1998; bars Efstathiou, Lake and Negroponte 1982. Tuned against Behroozi et al. 2019, Renzini and Peng 2015, Andrews and Martini 2013 and Madau and Dickinson 2014 (package log G3)
sources.rings: Multi-zone chemical evolution (Matteucci and Francois 1989; Chiappini et al. 1997, 2001); Kennicutt 1998 star formation with a Martin and Kennicutt 2001 threshold; Ia rate Maoz and Mannucci 2012 and Maoz and Graur 2017; solar mass fractions Asplund et al. 2009; radial winds Belfiore et al. 2019; inward drift Spitoni and Matteucci 2011; yields are IMF-integrated net yields in solar units, tuned (package log G3)
sources.envelope: Galaxy design section 7: rings interpolated in radius and time; log-spiral density wave (Lin and Shu 1964), pitch 12 degrees and pattern speed 25 km/s/kpc (rough Milky Way values); scale heights 100, 300 and 900 pc; sterilising distance 10 pc (Gehrels et al. 2003); lethal bursts within 2 kpc at low metallicity (Piran and Jimenez 2014; Graham and Fruchter 2013), burst yield tuned so the Sun now sees about 0.4 per Gyr; texture is keyed lognormal noise (sketch)
sources.green: Galactic habitable zone (Lineweaver, Fenner and Gibson 2004) as editable criteria: [Fe/H] -0.5 to +0.3 (giant-planet dominance above, Fischer and Valenti 2005), at most 4 sterilising supernovae and 3 lethal bursts per Gyr (Earth has lived through several), 4 Gyr of quiet for complex life
sources.stars: Kroupa 2001 IMF; lifetimes 10 Gyr M^-2.5; white dwarf masses Kalirai et al. 2008; multiplicity by primary mass Duchene and Kraus 2013; separations Raghavan et al. 2010 (log a about 1.7 +- 1.5 au); dispersions rising as age^0.40 (Holmberg, Nordstrom and Andersen 2009 section 6.3, total dispersion); midplane density 0.1 solar masses per pc^3 (McKee et al. 2015); cluster mass function M^-2 (Lada and Lada 2003, measured from 50 to 1000 solar masses with a drop below 50; used beyond that range as an extrapolation)
sources.nucleus: Eddington luminosity and Salpeter e-folding (Salpeter 1964, ApJ 140, 796, https://doi.org/10.1086/147973); radiative efficiency 0.1 from the Soltan argument (Soltan 1982, MNRAS 200, 115, https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/200.1.115; Yu and Tremaine 2002, https://doi.org/10.1046/j.1365-8711.2002.05532.x); thin disc peak temperature Shakura and Sunyaev 1973 (A&A 24, 337); radiatively inefficient flows below about alpha squared of Eddington, with L proportional to the rate squared there (Narayan and Yi 1995, ApJ 452, 710, https://doi.org/10.1086/176343; viscosity alpha 0.1 is pack data, so about 1%; Yuan and Narayan 2014, https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-astro-082812-141003, note the exact square holds only for weak electron heating); unified model Antonucci 1993 (https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.aa.31.090193.002353: orientation explains much, not all) and Urry and Padovani 1995 (https://doi.org/10.1086/133630); radio-loud share Best et al. 2005 section 3.3 fit, about 1.25% at 1e8 Msun rising as M^1.6, ceiling near 30% (https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2966.2005.09192.x); seeds Volonteri 2010 (https://doi.org/10.1007/s00159-010-0029-x), direct collapse in atomic-cooling haloes Bromm and Loeb 2003 (https://doi.org/10.1086/377529; their seeds are 1e6 Msun or more), heavy seed 1e5 Msun from the 1e4 to 1e6 range of Lodato and Natarajan 2006 (MNRAS 371, 1813) and Latif and Ferrara 2016 (PASA 33, e051), fudge F61; tidal disruption rate Stone and Metzger 2016 (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stv2281), Hills mass Hills 1975 (https://doi.org/10.1038/254295a0); merger delay is a rough dynamical-friction plus hardening time (sketch). Checked at source by the citations thread on 19 Nov 2026 except where marked (package log G-nuclei)
sources.origin: Reconstructed origins (top-level design 17.1): radial migration by churning at spiral corotation (Sellwood and Binney 2002, MNRAS 336, 785, https://doi.org/10.1046/j.1365-8711.2002.05806.x), guide-radius spread 3.6 kpc over 8 Gyr growing as sqrt(age) (Frankel et al. 2018, Measuring Radial Orbit Migration in the Galactic Disk, ApJ 865, 96, https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4357/aadba5); birthplaces weighted by the rings' star formation at birth; [Fe/H] scatter about the gas 0.1 dex as the stars' feh_scatter; flat rotation curve 220 km/s; the path is the drift's mean course, linear in time (sketch). References written from memory, to verify (package log T2-clock)
sources.events: Galaxy design section 9. Supernova and burst rates are the envelope's (G4, from the rings of section 6); remnant bubbles of tens of parsecs lasting about 1 Myr (a Sedov-Taylor remnant reaches about 50 pc at a few hundred km/s); neutron-star mergers per type Ia about 3e-5 against 5e-3 per year (merger rate Abbott et al. 2023, Phys. Rev. X 13, 011048; Ia rate Li et al. 2011, MNRAS 412, 1473); comet showers from passages inside about 10,000 au (Hills 1981, AJ 86, 1730); passage speeds Maxwellian about the envelope's mean (sketch); arm crossings from the envelope's density wave. References written from memory, to verify (package log G6)
